requirements.evidence: Contract met: enum CallMode (app/Enums/CallMode.php:7-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable CallNextTicket with the exact signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:27). Queue row locked and is_active read from DB inside the transaction (:32-39); ordering priority desc, issued_at asc, id asc (:87-90); modes via match (:79-85); fairness looks at last 3 by called_at desc, id desc and requires a waiting normal (:99-111); candidate locked and re-checked, skipped ids excluded on retry (:45-55); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id set and the model returned (:57-62); docs updated. Small doubt: the fairness history filters `where('status', TicketStatus::Called)` (:103) rather than `called_at` not null, so tickets that later move past `called` (if such statuses exist) would drop out of the 'last 3 called' history.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions as a single invokable class; reuses InactiveQueueException; tests first-class in tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] updated (CHANGELOG.md:9); docs/architecture.md and docs/business-rules.md updated. Deviations: the architecture.md TODO 'link the test covering the single-call invariant ... once implemented' (docs/architecture.md:196-197) is left stale although the tests now exist; marking logic is hand-rolled instead of reusing Ticket::call().

security.evidence: No HTTP/Livewire surface; authorization is explicitly out of scope and documented as such (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:23, docs/business-rules.md:224). No mass assignment: attributes set individually (:57-60). Row locks prevent double calls (:32-35, :46-49). No user input or output escaping concerns.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers ordering incl. id tie-break (:275-295 diff lines), returned model state (:297-311), other queues/already called (:313-323), empty queue, priority_only/normal_only incl. exceptions (:332-360), fairness trigger, 2-call non-trigger, reset by normal, no normal waiting, mode calls counting in history, called_at/id history ordering (:362-447), inactive and stale queue model (:449-475), concurrent call skip and only-candidate concurrent case via a retrieved hook (:477-516), write-once fields (:518-526). Minor: global helper functions `waiting()`/`called()` in a Pest file may collide with other test files.

simplicity.evidence: Compact action (~110 lines) with a small pick()/mustCallNormal() split and a named constant FAIRNESS_STREAK. Minor duplication: the 'mark called' assignments (:57-60) re-implement what Ticket::call() presumably already does; the skipped-ids loop is the minimum needed for rule 7.

readability.evidence: Clear names (pick, mustCallNormal, $lockedQueue, $skipped), PHPDoc on the public method and on helpers, comments explaining why the re-check exists (:41-42). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Diff touches only the action, enum, exception, its test, the two docs the task names, and CHANGELOG. Business-rules table annotations (docs/business-rules.md:208-209, 233) are related to the task.

issues.explanation: Fairness history only counts tickets whose current status is `called`; if tickets can move to later statuses, they would disappear from the 'last 3 called' history, so filtering on `called_at` not null would be more robust.
The TODO to link the single-call/concurrency test 'once implemented' is left in place even though this change adds those tests.
Marking the ticket called duplicates the existing Ticket::call() domain method instead of reusing it on the locked row.
Global helper functions `waiting()` and `called()` in a Pest file share the global namespace and can cause a redeclaration fatal if another test file defines the same names.
CallMode annotations are added to the Priority level table and only to the Next button row, which is inconsistent (Priority/Normal buttons are left unannotated).

review.summary: Adds CallMode, NoWaitingTicketsException and an invokable CallNextTicket action that locks the queue, reads is_active from the DB, picks a candidate with deterministic ordering and the 3-priority fairness rule, re-locks and re-checks the candidate, and marks it called; docs, changelog and a thorough Pest suite (including stale-queue and concurrent-call cases) are included. Only small issues remain (status-based fairness history, a stale TODO in architecture.md, not reusing Ticket::call()), so it is approvable with nits.
